examples.en: That painter lived in the countryside in his later years.
I'm saving money from now so my later years will be comfortable.
My grandfather's final years were not lonely.

examples.ko: 작가의 말년 작품은 아주 조용하고 깊어요.
examples.en: The author's late works are very quiet and deep.
I want to spend my last years happily.
He never stopped writing until the end of his life.

explain: '노년'은 나이 든 시기를 가리키고, '말년'은 삶이나 일의 마지막 시기를 가리켜요. 보통 '말년에'로 쓰고, 어르신 앞에서 '말년'이라고 하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 말년 병장이라서 요즘 일을 거의 안 해요.
phrases.en: a soldier near discharge who takes it easy
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 제대할 병장을 가리키는 군대 말이에요. 느긋하게 지내는 사람을 놀릴 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Military slang for a sergeant close to discharge; also used to tease someone who takes things easy.

explain_en: '노년' refers to old age, while '말년' points to the last stretch of a life or career. It is usually used as '말년에', and saying '말년' in front of an elderly person can be rude.

examples.en: This period was the heyday of Korean cinema's revival.
They say the 1990s were a golden revival period for Korean pop.
The city entered a period of revival, and people flocked to it.

examples.ko: 불교 문화의 부흥기에 많은 절이 지어졌어요.
examples.en: Many temples were built during the revival of Buddhist culture.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 요즘 새로운 부흥기를 누리고 있어요.
examples.en: That shop is enjoying a new boom these days.
Will a revival period come to our neighborhood again?

explain: '전성기'는 가장 잘나가던 때이고, '부흥기'는 약해졌다가 다시 힘차게 일어나는 시기에 더 잘 어울려요. 문화, 산업, 종교, 도시 이야기에 많이 쓰고 '맞이하다, 누리다'와 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: '전성기' is the peak time, while '부흥기' fits a time when something weak rises strongly again. It is common for culture, industry, religion and cities, and often goes with '맞이하다' and '누리다'.

examples.ko: 섣달이 되면 한 해가 다 갔다는 생각이 들어요.
examples.en: When Seotdal comes, I feel the year is nearly over.

examples.ko: 섣달 그믐날에는 가족이 모여 밤을 새웠어요.
examples.en: On the last night of Seotdal, the family gathered and stayed up all night.
The cold of Seotdal is truly biting.
It snowed a lot this Seotdal.
In Seotdal the market is crowded with Lunar New Year shoppers.
Once Seotdal passes, the new year comes soon.

explain: 음력 12월을 가리키는 옛 느낌의 말이에요. 보통 음력 마지막 날인 '섣달그믐'으로 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '12월'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is an old-fashioned word for the twelfth lunar month. It mostly appears in '섣달그믐' (the last day of the lunar year), and in daily talk people simply say '12월'.

examples.ko: 세밑이 가까워 오니 고향에 가고 싶은 마음이 간절해져요.
examples.en: As the end of the year draws near, I long more and more to go home.
The expressways are very congested at the end of the year.

examples.ko: 올해 세밑은 가족과 조용히 보낼 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to spend this year's end quietly with my family.

examples.ko: 세밑 분위기 때문인지 거리가 들떠 보여요.
examples.en: Maybe because of the year-end mood, the streets look excited.

examples.ko: 세밑에 이웃을 돕는 모금 활동이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many fundraising drives to help neighbors at the end of the year.
I called to give you my year-end greetings in advance.

explain: 한 해가 끝나 가는 12월 말쯤을 가리키고, '연말'보다 글이나 뉴스에서 좀 더 운치 있게 들려요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '연말'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It points to the last days of December as the year ends, and it sounds a bit more literary than '연말' in writing and news. In everyday conversation people usually just say '연말'.

examples.en: A year-end bell-ringing ceremony is held at Bosingak.

examples.ko: 송구영신 예배에 온 가족이 함께 갔어요.
examples.en: The whole family went to the New Year's Eve service together.

examples.ko: 송구영신이라는 말처럼 묵은해를 보내고 새해를 맞아요.
examples.en: As the phrase says, we send off the old year and welcome the new one.

examples.ko: 올해 송구영신은 집에서 조용히 보내고 싶어요.
examples.en: This year I want to spend New Year's Eve quietly at home.

examples.ko: 송구영신을 기념해 친구들과 해돋이를 보러 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: To mark the turn of the year, we decided to go watch the sunrise with friends.

examples.ko: 송구영신 인사를 보냈더니 친구가 바로 답장했어요.
examples.en: I sent a new year's greeting and my friend replied right away.

explain: 12월 31일 밤부터 새해로 넘어가는 때를 말하는 한자 성어예요. 타종 행사, 예배, 카드 문구처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '연말연시'나 '새해맞이'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is a Chinese-character phrase for the time when the year turns over from the night of December 31. It often appears in formal settings such as bell-ringing events, services and card messages. In everyday talk, people more often say '연말연시' or '새해맞이'.

examples.en: I sent a New Year's card to my teacher again this year.
A pretty New Year's card arrived from a friend.
I carefully wrote New Year's greetings in the card.
These days people send greetings by text instead of New Year's cards.
It's good to mail New Year's cards at the end of December.
I made a New Year's card with a family photo on it.

explain: 새해 인사를 적어 보내는 카드예요. '새해 복 많이 받으세요' 같은 인사를 많이 쓰고, 요즘은 종이 카드 대신 메시지나 사진으로 인사하는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It is a card you send with New Year's greetings. People often write something like '새해 복 많이 받으세요', and these days many send messages or images instead of paper cards.

en: May and June; May or June

examples.ko: 오뉴월 한낮에는 밖에 오래 못 있어요.
examples.en: At midday in early summer, I can't stay outside for long.
This year the rainy season has already started from early summer.

examples.ko: 오뉴월에는 해가 길어서 저녁 늦게까지 밝아요.
examples.en: In early summer the days are long, so it stays light until late evening.
The sunshine of early summer is much stronger than you'd think.

examples.ko: 오뉴월 땡볕 아래서 일하던 할머니가 생각나요.
examples.en: I think of my grandmother working under the scorching early-summer sun.
In the heat of early summer, you lose your appetite too.

explain: 원래 음력 오월과 유월을 합친 말이라 요즘 달력의 5~6월과 꼭 같지는 않지만, 초여름의 더위나 햇볕을 말할 때 '오뉴월 더위', '오뉴월 땡볕'처럼 많이 써요. 속담에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 오뉴월 감기는 개도 안 걸린다는데 저는 걸렸어요.
phrases.en: They say even a dog doesn't catch a cold in early summer, but I did.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여름에 감기에 걸린 사람을 조심성이 없거나 몸이 약하다고 놀릴 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb used to tease someone who catches a cold in summer, implying carelessness or weakness.
phrases.en_equiv: only the careless catch a summer cold

explain_en: It originally combines the fifth and sixth months of the lunar calendar, so it doesn't exactly match May and June on today's calendar, but it is commonly used for early-summer heat and sunshine, as in '오뉴월 더위' and '오뉴월 땡볕'. It also appears often in proverbs.

examples.en: They say autumn is the season of high skies and fat horses.
They say it's the season of high skies and big appetites, and my appetite is great lately.
With such a clear sky, I really feel the saying about autumn.

examples.ko: 천고마비 시즌에 맞춰 가을 축제가 열려요.
examples.en: An autumn festival is held in season.
Maybe because it's autumn, I keep craving snacks.
Blaming the autumn season, I overate again today.

explain: 가을을 말할 때 쓰는 사자성어예요. 하늘이 높고 맑으며 입맛이 좋아 살이 찐다는 농담과 함께 자주 나와요. 보통 '천고마비의 계절'이라는 형태로 말해요.
explain_en: It is a four-character expression used to talk about autumn. It often appears with the joke that the sky is high and clear and appetites grow, so people gain weight. It is usually said as '천고마비의 계절'.

examples.ko: 현생에서 못 이룬 꿈은 다음 생에 이루고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to achieve the dreams I could not fulfill in this life in the next one.

examples.ko: 요즘 현생을 사느라 바빠서 드라마를 못 봐요.
examples.en: I am busy living my real life these days, so I cannot watch dramas.

examples.ko: 현생이 너무 바빠서 취미 활동할 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: Real life is so busy that I have no time for my hobbies.

examples.ko: 이번 주는 현생에 집중해야 해서 모임에 못 가요.
examples.en: I have to focus on real life this week, so I cannot go to the meeting.
I think the relationships we have in this life are really precious.

examples.ko: 현생은 공부와 일로 정신없지만 주말에는 쉬어요.
examples.en: Real life is hectic with study and work, but I rest on weekends.

explain: 원래는 '이번 생'이라는 뜻으로 '전생', '내생'과 짝을 이뤄요. 요즘 인터넷에서는 취미나 덕질과 달리 학교·직장 같은 현실 생활을 가리키기도 해서, 친구끼리 가볍게 쓰는 말투예요.

phrases.example: 시험 기간이라 잠시 덕질을 쉬고 현생을 살고 있어요.
phrases.en: It is exam season, so I am taking a break from my fandom and living my real life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷에서 취미나 덕질을 잠시 접고 학교·직장 같은 현실의 일에 집중한다는 가벼운 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual internet expression for setting hobbies or fandom aside to focus on real-life duties like school or work.

explain_en: It originally means 'this life' and pairs with '전생' (past life) and '내생' (next life). Online these days it can also mean real life like school or work, as opposed to hobbies or fandom, in a casual tone among friends.
